question: An 18-year-old man comes to the physician because of severe left shoulder pain after a basketball match. During the game, the patient sustained an injury to the posterior part of his outstretched arm after being blocked by a defender. Examination shows no gross deformity of the left shoulder. Palpation of the shoulder elicits mild tenderness. Internal rotation of the arm against resistance shows weakness. These findings are most specific for injury to which of the following muscles?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Injury to the posterior part of the outstretched arm" -> "Weakness in internal rotation against resistance" -> "Specific for rotator cuff muscles" -> "Injury to the infraspinatus muscle" -> 80%
CHAIN: "Palpation elicits mild tenderness" -> "Weakness in internal rotation against resistance" -> "Specific for subscapularis muscle injury" -> 75%
analysis: Based on the patient's presentation of severe left shoulder pain, weakness with internal rotation, and tenderness on palpation, the most likely muscle injured is the infraspinatus.
